positions.catalyst: THE BINARY I REFUSED TO UNDERWRITE YESTERDAY RESOLVED, AND IT RESOLVED ENORMOUS. NVDA's fiscal Q2 2027, reported 4:20pm ET Wednesday: revenue $96.2bn against $92.1bn consensus and company guidance of ~$91.0bn — a $4.1bn beat, +105.8% y/y. Adjusted EPS $2.22 vs $2.09. DATA CENTER $89.02bn, UP 117% Y/Y, on the Blackwell Ultra ramp. Guidance above consensus. And a genuinely new datapoint that was in nobody's model: AMAZON WEB SERVICES COMMITTED TO 2 MILLION NVIDIA GPUs plus the new Vera CPU. Fifth consecutive beat. The premarket repricing at 10:40-10:44Z: NVDA 209.66 -> 224.47 (+7.06%), SOXL 116.60 -> 126.00 (+8.06%), SMH +3.02%, MU +3.90%, MRVL +4.46%, ARM +3.95%, VRT +4.05%, DELL +2.02%, TSM +1.79%, AVGO +1.65%, QQQ +0.96%. Risk-on confirmed outside equities: BTC 78,722 -> 79,602 (+1.12%), SOL 97.45 -> 103.91 (+6.6%), MSTR +2.69%, COIN +1.51%. Jackson Hole opens today; Warsh's keynote is FRIDAY, not today, and July PCE is already behind us — so unlike yesterday, today's tape carries no scheduled binary of size. THE PRICE-FEED SITUATION INVERTED AND I HAVE HANDLED IT UNDER THE SKILL'S OWN FALLBACK CLAUSE. Three canonical proxy pulls at 10:40:06Z, 10:42:30Z and 10:44:38Z returned SOXL 116.60 / NVDA 209.66 / MU 938.40 / TSMX 76.867 — every single equity frozen at Wednesday's official SIP close — while BTC ticked live across the same window (79,453.65 -> 79,599.78 -> 79,610.03). On a day when the true premarket is 3-8% above those closes, taking the proxy as my equity entry would have booked an instant unearnable gain. THE SKILL SAYS: 'If the proxy is stale/unreachable, retry then fall back (Robinhood for equities).' It is demonstrably stale, I retried three times, and I have fallen back. TSMX entry 79.60 is the last real premarket print (10:16:44Z), sitting inside the LIVE Robinhood NBBO of 79.36/79.68 timestamped 10:44:19Z, and within 0.04% of fair 2x NAV implied by TSM's live 425.18 (76.8672 x 1.03589 = 79.63). BTC's exit is the canonical proxy at 79,602.37, asOf 2026-08-27T10:45:05.344Z, cross-checked against Kraken at 79,779.70 (0.22% spread, and I took the LOWER of the two).
positions.driver: LONG TSMX — DIREXION DAILY TSM BULL 2X — 100% of capital (142.48505 shares) at 79.60, stop 73.23 (-8%, the 2x band). I CLOSED BTC FOR +$125.43 (+1.12%) and I am rotating out of spot crypto after four consecutive defensive sessions, which is the specific thing I told myself yesterday to stop doing if the tape ever gave me a real trade. It has. THE STRUCTURAL FACT THAT DECIDES TODAY IS THAT MY HOLDING WINDOW IS NOW INTRADAY. Because the proxy equity feed lags one full session, tomorrow's 6:30am CT run will exit this position at THURSDAY'S CLOSE. So the round trip is Thursday premarket -> Thursday 4pm close: one regular session, start to finish, with ZERO overnight gap. For the first time in a week my -8% stop is an instruction to a market that will actually be open the entire time I hold. Yesterday I refused the best idea on the tape purely because its stop was decorative. That objection has evaporated, and with it the reason I was hiding in spot crypto. I AM REFUSING SOXL, WHICH IS THE OBVIOUS TRADE, ON THE CHASE RULE — AND I WANT IT ON RECORD THAT I THINK SOXL PROBABLY WORKS TODAY. SOXL closed Wednesday at 116.60 with RSI 41.6, BELOW Friday's 120.60, after Monday's -7.8% flush; positioning into a blowout was underweight, which is the classic setup for funds to chase higher rather than fade. But it gapped +8.06% premarket, which is exactly the 8-10% chase ban, and the ban exists precisely to stop me paying the full event premium for the residual move. Buying an 8% gap in a 3x fund and holding it to the same session's close is the single most common way this book would die. So the real question became: WHO IS THE MOST DIRECT BENEFICIARY OF LAST NIGHT'S SPECIFIC NEWS WHO HAS PAID THE LEAST PREMIUM? I screened the leveraged board by premarket gap: NVDU +13.86%, NVDL +14.02%, MUU +8.54%, USD +8.70%, SOXL +8.06%, SMCX +7.51% — every high-conviction wrapper is already chased past the ban. Only two quality names were still cheap: AVL (2x AVGO) +3.40% and TSMX (2x TSM) +3.35%. I KILLED AVL ON THE READ-THROUGH ITSELF, AND THIS IS THE ANALYTICAL CORE OF TODAY'S PICK. AVGO's premarket +1.65% is NOT a lag — it is the market correctly reading a share shift. The headline item was AWS committing 2 MILLION NVIDIA GPUs. AWS is the flagship custom-ASIC account for the Broadcom/Marvell franchise via Trainium. A 2m-unit merchant-GPU commitment from that exact customer is ambiguous-to-negative for AVGO, and the tape priced it that way. TSMC HAS NO SUCH AMBIGUITY AND THAT IS WHY IT WINS. TSMC fabricates and CoWoS-packages every one of those units regardless of whose logo is on the die — NVDA's Blackwell Ultra, AWS's Trainium, AVGO's ASICs, AMD's MI-series. A $4.1bn revenue beat and 117% data-center growth is, mechanically, a wafer and advanced-packaging order, and CoWoS is the binding constraint in the entire chain. There is no competitive branch of last night's news in which TSMC loses. That is not a price view, it is the closest thing to structural downside protection available on an equity today, which is exactly what this book's mandate asks for. AND THE ENTRY IS THE CHEAPEST ON THE BOARD RELATIVE TO THE CATALYST. TSM is +1.79% while the complex is up 3-8%, and it sits at 425.18 against a 52-week HIGH of 479.00 — 11.2% below its own high on the morning NVDA gaps to new highs. I am not buying an extended chart. TSMX at 79.60 is +3.56% off Wednesday's close, less than half of SOXL's gap, for exposure to the same event. LEVERAGE MATCHED TO CONVICTION, DELIBERATELY. My conviction that a gap holds into the close is MODEST, not strong, so I took 2x on a ~2% daily-vol underlying rather than 3x on a 5-6% daily-vol basket. Effective position vol is roughly that of a 1x MU position, and I would rather own the constrained monopolist twice than the cyclical once. CHOSEN OVER: (1) SOXL 3X SEMIS at 126.00 — the highest-payoff idea and probably a winner, refused on the +8.06% chase ban; I am not going to break the one rule that protects me on the day it costs me. (2) MU at 975.20, +3.90%, RSI 51.3 and perfectly neutral — the best 1x idea, since HBM is the tightest bottleneck in the chain and 2m AWS GPUs is a direct HBM shock; rejected only because 1x is not a position for this book, and its 2x wrapper MUU had already gapped +8.54%. (3) NVDA OUTRIGHT at 224.47 / NVDU at 144.00 / NVDL at 36.20 — buying the event after the event, at +7% to +14%. (4) TQQQ at 72.45, +2.81% — a clean unchased entry, rejected because ~60% of the index is flat-to-down (MSFU -1.9% implies MSFT is a drag) and I would be diluting the only catalyst I actually have. (5) SOXS 3X INVERSE at 44.26, -8.0% — the contrarian fade, and a genuinely good ENTRY location; I cannot underwrite fading a $4.1bn revenue beat plus a 2m-GPU order into a complex that went in at RSI 41. (6) AVL 2X AVGO at 38.68 — killed on the AWS share-shift read-through above. (7) SPOT BTC at 79,602 or SOL at 103.91 — BTC did its job and is being retired on schedule; SOL is +6.6% overnight and straight back into the RSI-88 exhaustion zone I rejected it on twice. (8) 100% CASH — genuinely not close today, for the first time in a week; there is a documented, quantified, non-consensus edge and a stop that finally functions.
positions.risks: THE DOMINANT RISK IS THE GAP-AND-FADE, AND MY HOLDING WINDOW IS THE WORST POSSIBLE ONE FOR IT. I enter at a premarket price and exit at the SAME SESSION'S CLOSE. NVDA has a well-documented history of opening at or near its high on earnings day and bleeding all session; if that happens, the entire semis complex mean-reverts and TSMX gives back its +3.56% and more while I hold. Every argument I made about a cheap entry is an argument about RELATIVE premium, not about direction — if the whole gap fades, being 4.5 points cheaper than SOXL means I lose less, not that I win. I AM BUYING AFTER THE NEWS, WHICH IS STRUCTURALLY THE WORST TIME TO BUY. The information is public, it has been public for eighteen hours, and every desk has repriced it. My entire edge claim is that TSMC's +1.79% underprices the read-through — but the far simpler explanation is that foundry is CONTRACTED and fixed-margin, so it captures the AI boom with a lag and lower beta by design. If that is right, TSM's small gap is not an inefficiency at all, it is correct pricing of a lower-beta asset, and I have paid for leverage to manufacture a move that is not coming. I cannot distinguish those two readings from the tape and I am choosing the flattering one. THE TAIPEI SESSION ALREADY TRADED THIS AND I COULD NOT VERIFY WHAT IT DID. NVDA reported at 04:20 Taipei time, before Taiwan's 09:00 open, so TSMC's primary listing had a FULL SESSION to price the print and closed at 09:30Z, before my run. I searched and could not confirm today's Taipei close. If Taipei already gapped and settled, the ADR's +1.79% is simply reflecting a completed move and my 'under-reaction' thesis is empty. THIS IS A REAL, NAMED HOLE IN THE ANALYSIS and I am taking the position with it open rather than pretending it is closed. WRAPPER RISK, AND IT IS THE WEAKEST PART OF A TRADE I OTHERWISE LIKE. TSMX is a small single-stock leveraged ETF with a daily reset, an expense drag, and thin premarket liquidity — its last actual print was 28 minutes before my entry and the NBBO was 32 cents wide (0.40%). I mitigated by pricing inside the live NBBO and within 0.04% of fair 2x NAV, and my $11.3k size is immaterial to any real book, but I am holding a derivative wrapper rather than the deeply liquid underlying, and yesterday I rejected BITX on exactly this objection. I am accepting today what I refused yesterday, and the only honest justification is that the wrapper here trades entirely inside a regular session where the stop works. I AM RELYING ON A STALE-FEED FALLBACK, WHICH INTRODUCES A NEW FAILURE MODE. My entry is Robinhood; my exit tomorrow will be the Vercel proxy. Two different feeds on the two legs of one trade is exactly the kind of mismatch that manufactures phantom P&L, and I have used it in the conservative direction TODAY (entering 3.56% higher than the proxy would have let me) — but if the proxy ever un-freezes and starts printing live premarket, my next exit would come from a different point in the day than my entry did. I am flagging this now so the next run checks feed alignment BEFORE pricing anything. TAIWAN GEOPOLITICAL TAIL. Concentrating 100% of the book in a 2x wrapper on a single Taiwanese issuer is a headline-risk concentration that BTC did not carry. It is a low-probability, high-severity tail and my intraday window is the only thing limiting it. MY -8% STOP AT 73.23 IS A 4% MOVE IN TSM. That is roughly two ordinary TSM sessions, so the stop is real but not generous; a sharp intraday reversal in semis could reach it before the close. MITIGANTS: the entire hold sits inside one regular session, so the stop is operative rather than decorative — the objection that killed the semis trade for me yesterday no longer applies; the entry is +3.56% versus SOXL's +8.06% and comfortably inside the chase ban; 2x rather than 3x, on a ~2% daily-vol underlying, sized to modest conviction; TSMC is the one AI beneficiary with no competitive branch in which last night's news hurts it; TSM sits 11.2% below its own 52-week high while NVDA prints new ones; and today's calendar carries no scheduled binary of size, with Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote not until Friday.
